text: Shadowbans, shadowbans, shadowbans. I have been getting those quite a bit lately. But yesterday on TikTok I got the biggest one in a while. So if you are waiting for my response to Professor Neil's claim number 2, that more than 1 in 3 men SA women, it's on the channel since yesterday. But most probably, it didn't show up on your FYP. You literally need to go to my page to watch it. Normally, my FYP traffic is around 85-90%, like on the left slide here. But look at the right slide. FYP crashed to 33%, with most views coming from people going directly to my profile. Because of this shadowban, I need to chill with debates for a bit, to reset my algorithm. I have no proof, this is only speculation. But it could be the case that my opponents, instead of responding to my videos debunking theirs, decided it would be easier to just report my content. It is sad, but it is what it is. Also, in case something actually happens to my TikTok, so you do not lose me, because who knows, subscribe to my Instagram. My username is on the screen, or you can find it by clicking the link in the bio. But if I cannot normally debate right now, let me talk about debating itself. I often get messages from you guys asking me how to learn to debate, where to start, how do I do it. For example, one of you recently wrote, I have always wanted to dialogue in your way, having debates on serious themes, but I am just 18 and my Italian family and friends are not willing to. What are your tips? Never heard of an Italian family that doesn't want to debate something, but okay, let me try to share my thoughts. Honestly, it is not that easy for me to answer this question, because I never really learned how to do it the proper way. I was never part of a debate club, never in a political organization, nothing like that. Also, if it would come down to live debates, I would probably be much worse. So guys, do not overestimate me. But overall, at least partly, my ability to express myself the way I do comes from the fact that I'm simply a bit older than many of you guys. And life gave me opportunities to learn different things. Living in different regions of the world exposed me to different ideas, cultures, and ways of thinking. I already mentioned this before, I am originally from Kazakhstan. As a teenager, I moved to the US, did my bachelor's there, and then worked in finance. Now I'm in Germany, where I moved more than five years ago to do my master's, and now I still work in finance here. Yes, I currently have a full-time job. Content creation is kind of my hobby that I do in my free time, but I do have it as a goal to eventually make it my main thing. But you see, I kind of have always been curious. I like talking to people, sometimes debating them, but also genuinely trying to understand their viewpoints. It was a gradual process that led me to where I am right now. So when I debate today, I try to do my research, ideally to understand both sides of the argument, and then I let that research and preparation do its job. That is the result you see on your screen. Also, unlike so many people who grow up and stay in their bubbles today, I was constantly challenged on my views and beliefs. At some point, I realized that it's very rare for something to be just black or white. Nuance and context matter a lot. It doesn't mean I do not have strong opinions. I do, especially when it comes to relationship topics or self-respect and personal boundaries. But still, it doesn't change the fact that, in general, you should try to stay open-minded, objective, and unbiased. So naturally, I started challenging different ideas that came my way. Left, right, democratic, socialist, male or female, it didn't matter. And naturally, I would end up in debates, because my views were often different from the people around me. But I was also curious about their views. I also realized that to articulate yourself well, you need to understand your opponent. You need to put yourself in their shoes and sometimes understand their point better than they do. That is how you can spot the flaws or recognize the strong parts. So overall, honestly, I'm probably not the best person to ask how to learn debating. I kind of just learned it on the go. There are more experienced people out there who can probably help you with that better. But if you like my style, you can just watch my videos and try to follow a similar approach.
